item.title: In Canada: Drake Breaks Records for Most No. 1s Ever on the Billboard Canadian Hot 100 & Album Charts
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: "Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest news and trends in the music industry. Today, we're talking about a major milestone for Drake, the Toronto-born rapper who's breaking records left and right on the Billboard Canadian charts."
[Short music transition]
Host: "Drake's recent release, Iceman, has catapulted him to new heights, with his song 'Janice STFU' becoming his 14th number one hit on the Canadian Hot 100 chart. This feat breaks a tie with Justin Bieber and Taylor Swift for the most number one songs in Canadian Hot 100 history. And if that's not impressive enough, Drake is also dominating the top 10, occupying 9 out of the top 10 spots simultaneously."
[Short music transition]
Host: "But that's not all - Drake has also broken another record held by Taylor Swift, charting 17 songs in the top 20 simultaneously. He's had an astonishing 51 tracks in the top five and 84 tracks that have hit the top 10, extending his personal records. And to top it all off, Drake has a whopping 42 out of 100 chart spots on this week's Canadian Hot 100, surpassing Morgan Wallen's record of 37 tracks."
[Short music transition]
Host: "In other news, the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission, or CRTC, has announced an update to its streaming regulations. The CRTC has increased its base contributions for major audiovisual streaming services, requiring platforms earning over $25 million in revenue to pay 15% of their income to Canadian content funds. This move aims to support Canadian and Indigenous content, and ensure that Canadian stories continue to be told and made available to audiences across the country."
[Short music transition]
Host: "So, what does this mean for music streaming? While the CRTC's update focuses on audiovisual streaming services, it's likely that music streaming platforms will be impacted in the future. We'll be keeping a close eye on developments and bringing you updates as more information becomes available."
[Outro music plays]
Host: "Thanks for tuning in to our podcast. Join us next time for more news and updates from the music industry."
